names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 16 aprilie, «Sfintele Mucenițe fecioare Agapia, Irina și Hionia».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 16 Απριλίου, «Αγίες Αγάπη, Ειρήνη και Χιονία», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's heading for the Julian 16 April, „Св. муч. Агапија, Хионија и Ирина.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and without муч., which is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types`. One rank word stands over the whole company and belongs to none of them, so what is left for this saint is the bare forename; the heading gives no epithet, no city and no see, and the companionship clause this corpus keeps in some of these display names is not part of the source's name for anybody. No other folder in the corpus holds this Serbian form.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 16 aprilie — «Sfintele Mucenițe fecioare Agapia, Irina și Hionia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 16ης Απριλίου — «Αγίες Αγάπη, Ειρήνη και Χιονία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 16 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps the three sisters on, and it names the same three: the persecution under Maximian, the flight to a high mountain, the arrest in 304 and the trial before the ruler Dulcitius. **The two calendars disagree about where they belonged.** saint.gr calls them «πνευματικά βλαστάρια της Εκκλησίας της Θεσσαλονίκης», spiritual shoots of the Church of Thessalonica, where the Romanian notice on which this folder's display name rests has them of Aquileia; the source's reading is recorded here and the corpus's own name and dates are left alone. saint.gr gives the year of the arrest, 304, and the page's heading repeats it beside each name as «(; - 304)». saint.gr has Agape and Chionia die in the fire and Irene by a soldier's arrow after being shut in a brothel, which is not quite the Romanian notice's order; the source's reading is in the life paragraph and neither account has been made to yield to the other. The corpus holds eight folders whose names fold onto Agape and none of them is this woman.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 29.04.2026 (16. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Агапија, Хионија и Ирина.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, an enumerated company of three sisters, so one row per woman, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep them on. The entry is the fullest account of them in any source read for this folder and four things in it are new to the corpus: that Irene answered the emperor to his face that it is foolish to bow to things of stone and wood, ordered for an agreed price and made by the hands of some mortal man; that the commander Dulcitius, meaning to defile the virgins, lost his mind at the door of their prison while they were praying and embraced and kissed the black cauldrons and pots standing there, going away sooty and black; that angels turned back the soldiers taking Irene to the brothel and set her on a hill the commander could not climb; and that Anastasia gathered all three bodies into one place and buried them honourably. It calls the trial a trial before the emperor himself, where the Romanian notice has the governor alone. **The year is new to this folder**: „Све чесно пострадаше за Христа Цара и Господа око 304. год.“, about 304, and it agrees with the 304 the Greek page gives for the arrest, so nothing was displaced. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintelor Mucenițe fecioare Agapia, Irina, Hionia», Glasul 4; the reading «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their struggles have won from Thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Thy strength, they overthrew their tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ὡς αὐτάδελφοι Κόραι καὶ οὐρανόφρονες, πρὸς εὐσέβειας ἀγῶνας ὁμονοούσαι καλῶς, τὸν ἀρχέκακον ἐχθρὸν κατεπαλαίσατε, Χιονὶα ἡ σεμνή, σὺν Ἀγάπη τὴ κλυτή, Εἰρήνη ἡ πανολβία. Καὶ νῦν Χριστὸν δυσωπεῖτε, ἐλεηθήναι τᾶς ψυχᾶς ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον, on the page of Αγίες Αγάπη, Ειρήνη και Χιονία. It is the three sisters' own and names all three.

english.text: As sisters born of one womb and heavenly-minded maidens, being rightly of one mind in the struggles for godliness, you wrestled down the enemy who is the author of evil: Chionia the modest, with Agape the renowned, and Irene the all-blessed. And now entreat Christ that our souls may find mercy.

hymns.text: Τά θαύματα τῶν ἁγίων σου Μαρτύρων, τεῖχος ἀκαταμάχητον ῆμῖν δωρησάμενος, Χριστέ ὁ Θεός, ταῖς αὐτῶν ἱκεσίαις, βουλάς ἐθνῶν διασκέδασον, τῆς βασιλείας τά σκῆπτρα κραταίωσον, ὡς μόνος ἀγαθός καὶ φιλάνθρωπος.

source.text: saint.gr — Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’, on the page of Αγίες Αγάπη, Ειρήνη και Χιονία. This is the common apolytikion of martyrs and names nobody; the page prints it under their names, so it is copied whole as the page has it.

english.text: Having given us the wonders of thy holy martyrs as an unassailable wall, O Christ God, at their supplications scatter the counsels of the nations and strengthen the sceptres of the kingdom, as thou alone art good and the lover of mankind.

hymns.text: Παρθενίας έσοπτρα, φωτοειδή πεφυκυίαι, νοερώς ηστράψατε, αθλητικάς λαμπηδόνας, πάσαν μέν, την Εκκλησίαν αγλαϊζούσας, νύκτα δέ, των νοσημάτων απελαυνούσας, Χιονία και Αγάπη, συν τη Ειρήνη, Χριστού κειμήλια.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, on the page of Αγίες Αγάπη, Ειρήνη και Χιονία. It is their own and names all three.

english.text: Being mirrors of virginity and shining with light, you flashed out spiritually the brightnesses of the contest, which make the whole Church glorious and drive away the night of sicknesses: Chionia and Agape, with Irene, treasures of Christ.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue for 16. април ст. ст.: „Све чесно пострадаше за Христа Цара и Господа око 304. год.“ — all suffered honourably for Christ the King and Lord about the year 304. The folder held no `dates` before this. It agrees with saint.gr, which this folder's own Greek citation records as putting the arrest in 304; doxologia's notice gives no year at all, naming only Diocletian. No year of birth is recorded anywhere read.
